questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

What should an author presentation do before the excerpt is read?

answer.text: A. Avoid giving any context at all.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs enough context to understand the excerpt.

answer.text: B. Explain every event in the full story.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Too much summary can take over the presentation.

answer.text: C. Introduce the title, genre, brief context, and listening focus.

feedback.text: Correct. These elements prepare the audience to understand the work.

answer.text: D. Apologize for the piece before reading.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presenter should guide the audience confidently and clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which statement best identifies presentation purpose?

answer.text: A. I want the audience to understand how my revised dialogue shows tension.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a clear craft-focused purpose.

answer.text: B. I want to talk until time runs out.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not a learning or presentation purpose.

answer.text: C. I want to avoid explaining the piece.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The standard requires communication of creative work.

answer.text: D. I want the audience to guess everything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. An author presentation should guide understanding. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

A student chooses a long chapter that requires ten minutes of plot explanation. What is the best revision to the plan?

answer.text: A. Keep the whole chapter because longer is always stronger.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Long excerpts can weaken focus. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Select a shorter excerpt that shows the key craft choice with brief context.

feedback.text: Correct. A focused excerpt better supports craft reasoning.

answer.text: C. Remove all context and hope the audience follows.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience still needs a clear frame.

answer.text: D. Replace the presentation with a written quiz.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The task is author presentation planning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which choice is plot summary instead of craft reasoning?

answer.text: A. I used repeated s sounds to slow the poem's ending.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is craft reasoning because it names sound and effect.

answer.text: B. I revised dialogue so the reader can infer discomfort.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is craft reasoning because it connects revision to effect.

answer.text: C. I placed the final image alone so the audience pauses.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This explains line break effect. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. The character leaves home, meets a friend, and returns later.

feedback.text: Correct. This tells events but does not explain writer choices.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which speaking note style best supports a presentation?

answer.text: A. Short key phrases in the planned sequence.

feedback.text: Correct. Key phrases help the presenter remember ideas while still addressing the audience.

answer.text: B. A full essay copied word for word in tiny font.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This can lead to flat reading and lost audience contact.

answer.text: C. No notes at all even if the sequence is complex.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Notes help maintain organization. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Random words with no connection to the excerpt.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Notes should support the plan. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Why should the presenter name a listening focus?

answer.text: A. It replaces the need to read the excerpt.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The focus prepares the excerpt; it does not replace it.

answer.text: B. It allows the presenter to skip craft reasoning.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presenter still needs to explain the choice after the excerpt.

answer.text: C. It tells the audience what craft choice to notice during the excerpt.

feedback.text: Correct. A listening focus guides attention and supports understanding.

answer.text: D. It hides the purpose from the audience.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It clarifies purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which is the strongest craft explanation?

answer.text: A. I wrote a poem because poems are short.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain a specific craft choice.

answer.text: B. I placed the final line by itself so the reader pauses before the speaker's decision.

feedback.text: Correct. This names a line break choice and explains reader effect.

answer.text: C. I like the ending most.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Preference is not craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. My story has an ending.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general to show craft reasoning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which revision reflection is strongest?

answer.text: A. I fixed stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and does not identify growth.

answer.text: B. I changed nothing and learned nothing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show process reflection. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I made it better somehow.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague for mastery. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I revised the opening image to establish setting before conflict, which makes the scene easier to enter.

feedback.text: Correct. This names a revision and explains its effect.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which sequence best matches the lesson presentation structure?

answer.text: A. Title and genre, context, listening focus, excerpt, craft reasoning, revision reflection.

feedback.text: Correct. This sequence prepares, presents, explains, and reflects.

answer.text: B. Excerpt, unrelated story, apology, ending.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This lacks clear framing and craft reasoning.

answer.text: C. Full plot summary, full draft history, no excerpt.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs focused presentation of the work.

answer.text: D. Title only, then stop.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A presentation needs more than identification. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

A presenter says, "This is a poem about rain." What should be added to improve the plan?

answer.text: A. A longer unrelated biography.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Extra unrelated information does not strengthen the craft focus.

answer.text: B. A craft focus, such as image, sound, line break, or tone.

feedback.text: Correct. Topic alone is not enough; the audience needs craft direction.

answer.text: C. A statement that no one needs context.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience benefits from useful framing. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. A promise that the poem has no choices.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Creative work is built from choices. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which excerpt is easiest for an audience to understand?

answer.text: A. A section that starts mid-conflict with no names, no context, and unclear speakers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This would require too much guessing. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. The entire portfolio read without pause.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is too broad for a focused presentation.

answer.text: C. A focused section introduced with a brief explanation of situation and speaker.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives the audience enough information to follow.

answer.text: D. A section the presenter cannot explain.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presenter must be able to explain craft choices.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which statement best communicates author growth?

answer.text: A. My first draft explained the fear directly; my revision used action so readers could infer it.

feedback.text: Correct. This compares draft and revision while explaining reader effect.

answer.text: B. I wrote it the night before.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain creative growth. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I did not revise anything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show process development. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. The assignment was difficult.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Difficulty alone does not describe growth in the work.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

What is the role of audience frame?

answer.text: A. It hides the title from the audience.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The title should usually be clear. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. It replaces the excerpt.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The frame supports the excerpt. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. It lists unrelated facts about the writer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The frame should connect to the work.

answer.text: D. It gives readers or listeners the context they need before the excerpt.

feedback.text: Correct. Audience frame prepares the audience without overexplaining.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

A student's presentation notes include only "read poem, done." What is missing?

answer.text: A. More silence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Silence does not replace planning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Title, context, listening focus, craft reasoning, and reflection.

feedback.text: Correct. These elements are needed for a complete author presentation plan.

answer.text: C. Random decoration.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration does not build presentation content. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. A hidden file name.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The issue is missing presentation structure. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which choice best explains why an excerpt should not require too much setup?

answer.text: A. Context is never allowed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Brief context is important. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Long setup proves the piece is complex.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Complexity does not excuse unclear presentation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. The audience should spend most of the presentation understanding the work and craft, not sorting through long background.

feedback.text: Correct. Brief context keeps the presentation focused. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. The presenter should avoid all explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Craft explanation is required. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which closing statement best fits an author presentation?

answer.text: A. This revision helped the final scene feel more tense because the reader now infers the conflict through dialogue.

feedback.text: Correct. This closes by connecting revision, craft, and effect.

answer.text: B. That is all, and I do not know why I picked it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This weakens purpose and reflection. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I hope it was not confusing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A stronger close explains the work's effect.

answer.text: D. The story is over.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not reflect on craft or growth.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which question should guide excerpt selection?

answer.text: A. Is this excerpt the longest possible?

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length does not guarantee quality. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Can I avoid talking about the excerpt?

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presenter must discuss the excerpt. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Will this confuse the audience?

feedback.text: Incorrect. Confusion is not the goal. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Does this excerpt show a craft choice I can explain clearly?

feedback.text: Correct. The excerpt should support craft reasoning. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which presentation plan best avoids summary-only speaking?

answer.text: A. List every event in order and stop.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is summary-only. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Name two craft choices and explain how each affects the reader.

feedback.text: Correct. This moves beyond plot into author reasoning.

answer.text: C. Read the entire piece without any introduction.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs frame and focus. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Say the piece is good without evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evaluation needs craft evidence. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which detail belongs in brief context before an excerpt?

answer.text: A. Every assignment the student completed all semester.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is too broad and unrelated to the immediate excerpt.

answer.text: B. A list of favorite songs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not frame the creative work.

answer.text: C. The speaker has just missed the last bus and is deciding whether to call home.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives the situation needed to understand the excerpt.

answer.text: D. A full explanation of the ending before reading.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Too much context can reduce the excerpt's impact.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which answer best describes communication of craft reasoning?

answer.text: A. Explaining how specific writing choices shape meaning or audience effect.

feedback.text: Correct. Craft reasoning connects choice to effect. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Saying the piece is finished.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Completion is not craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Listing page numbers only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Page numbers do not explain effect. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Avoiding all terms from the lesson.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Craft vocabulary helps explanation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

A presenter plans to discuss five unrelated craft choices in two minutes. What should the presenter do?

answer.text: A. Speak faster and keep all five.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Speed can reduce clarity. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Choose two or three focused points that connect to the purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. A focused plan is clearer and more teachable.

answer.text: C. Remove the excerpt to make room.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The excerpt is central to the presentation.

answer.text: D. Add more unrelated points.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This would increase confusion. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which phrase best signals a listening focus?

answer.text: A. Listen to everything and nothing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague to guide attention.

answer.text: B. I have no focus for this excerpt.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A planned presentation needs focus. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Ignore the language choices.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Craft choices are central to the presentation.

answer.text: D. Listen for the repeated hard consonant sounds in the final stanza.

feedback.text: Correct. This tells the audience exactly what craft choice to notice.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which statement is too vague for mastery?

answer.text: A. I used dialogue to reveal tension between the characters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a specific craft claim. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I revised sentence length to change pacing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This names a craft revision. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I made it better.

feedback.text: Correct. This does not identify what changed or how it affects the audience.

answer.text: D. I selected the excerpt because it shows the narrator's voice.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This explains selection with craft purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

What should the presenter practice for timing and clarity?

answer.text: A. Only the final word.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The full presentation needs practice. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. A different assignment.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Practice should match the presentation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Avoiding the excerpt completely.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The excerpt is part of the presentation.

answer.text: D. The sequence of title, context, excerpt, craft explanation, and reflection.

feedback.text: Correct. Practicing the sequence helps the presentation stay organized.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which final plan best meets the lesson standard?

answer.text: A. A plan with title, genre, brief context, selected excerpt, listening focus, craft reasoning, and revision reflection.

feedback.text: Correct. This includes the key author presentation elements.

answer.text: B. A plan that only says the work is creative.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not enough for presentation mastery.

answer.text: C. A plan with no excerpt and no craft explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The standard requires presenting and explaining creative work.

answer.text: D. A plan that only summarizes the plot.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Plot summary alone does not communicate craft reasoning.
